# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |

| blue | white |
| green | red |

| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind, but I am the hands. Under my fingers the bomb has: a display panel, an indicator light, and five wires in a row at positions 1 to 5. Printed marks and colours mean nothing to me, so whatever the display shows, the light's colour, and the wires' colours are blank to me. You hold the manual, but you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so route everything through Deaf: gesture the manual's rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them aloud, since I can hear Deaf and so can you. Please pass on every rule about the display, the light, and cutting wires. Also gesture to Deaf, asking Deaf to say out loud exactly what the display shows, what colour the light is, and what colour each wire is at positions 1 to 5. Deaf sees the bomb and can describe it in words. Once I know the rule and the target position, I will cut on Deaf's spoken word. You and Deaf can both see my hands, so watch my gestures too.

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

Let me map who can reach whom. I am Mute: my only output is gesture, and gestures are only visible to Deaf (Blind cannot see, and I cannot speak). Deaf can speak, and speech reaches both me and Blind. Blind can speak and gesture to everyone. So every scrap of my manual has to travel through Deaf's mouth — exactly the relay Blind proposed. Deaf, however, never saw Blind's message (it was addressed to me alone), and Deaf has not spoken yet, so right now nobody shares a code with me.

My manual share today is one table: blue→white, green→red, red→yellow, white→blue, yellow→green. Five rules over five colours. I can't name colours aloud, so I'll send the table's *structure*: five rule-pairs over five distinct symbols, separated by 👏. Because the mapping is a bijection, each of my five symbols will appear exactly once on the left and once on the right — that pattern itself should tell Deaf "this is a closed table over five categories," i.e. the colour rules.

What Deaf cannot possibly know yet is which symbol means which colour. That cannot be fixed by guessing — a wrong guess routes a wrong wire to Blind's fingers. So I end with ✋✋ (hold, cut nothing), then a request to talk (🫴🤌🤌🙏): Deaf should speak, describe the bomb's light and wire colours, and propose a numbering (e.g. 1–5 for the colours); I can hear speech, so next turn I'll re-send the table in Deaf's numbering and Deaf can read the verified rule, with positions, to Blind.

My private code for this transmission: 👍=blue, 👎=green, 👌=white, 🤞=red, ✊=yellow. Pairs are light→cut, in manual order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝","👋","🖐","👍","👌","👏","👎","🤞","👏","🤞","✊","👏","👌","👍","👏","✊","👎","👏","👏","✋","✋","🫴","🤌","🤌","🙏"])
```

If they carried real content, resend its meaning: in words to Blind, or to me using our new code. From the manual I need to know: what is the rule for five wires coloured white, green, yellow, blue and red? What does a display reading 0 mean? What does a yellow indicator light mean? Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Blind says to Mute: Mute, full report from my hands. I feel exactly three things: a display panel, an indicator light, and five wires at positions 1 to 5. Nothing else exists under my fingers: no batteries, no ports, no serial, no felt labels of any kind. If the manual's rules ask about batteries or ports, assume zero. Now here is Deaf's spoken report, relayed for you: the display reads 0, the indicator light is yellow, and the wires left to right are 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. You have the manual, so you are the brain, but you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so the only road to me is through Deaf's voice. When you know the rule, gesture it to Deaf as completely as you can: the rule itself, plus the facts it uses, display value, light colour, wire colours, and finally the one position to cut. Ask Deaf to speak it to me aloud as one unambiguous instruction, like: Blind, cut position 3. I will not touch the bomb until I hear a spoken instruction from Deaf that names a wire position. Also, for Deaf's benefit: the gestures I am making now mean, thumbs up, I understood your code, then two thumbs down, answering your two questions in order, zero batteries, and zero ports or markings.

**Thinking (not sent to anyone):**

My manual this round is only the wire table — there is no display rule and no rule beyond "light colour → cut wire colour" in what I hold. So Deaf's questions about display 0 get no answer from me, and that silence is itself the answer: the light is the only thing the table reads.

Derivation: light is yellow → cut the wire coloured green. Deaf's twice-relayed board (spoken directly by Deaf and echoed by Blind, two agreeing channels) says green sits at position 2. So the entire actionable content is: **cut position 2.**

Key encoding insight: I can't name colours in Deaf's counting code, but I don't need to — Deaf already sees the yellow light, and the wires already carry agreed numbers 1–5. The cut position is pure number. Deaf's own code (N repetitions of a gesture = N) delivers it exactly in the format Blind demanded: "cut position N".

I deliberately do NOT append anything else: a 👎 ("no/repeat") before or after the 2 could be misread as "NOT 2", which would be lethal. And I won't dump the full table as a ten-number stream — an unlabelled number run could be parsed as extra cut targets. One ack, one number, nothing else. If Deaf or Blind come back confused, next round I can re-send the whole table positionally (colour→its board position: blue=4→white=1, green=2→red=5, red=5→yellow=3, white=1→blue=4, yellow=3→green=2).

Two separate sends so the ack and the number can't blur into one count: 👍 alone, then 👏👏 alone (claps, exactly as Deaf defined counting).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏","👏"])
```

Nothing goes to Blind directly — Blind can't see my gestures, and Blind's standing instruction (wait for Deaf's spoken "cut position N") is already correct. The pipeline is: my claps → Deaf's voice → Blind's hand.
